scope: Proposition 4.7 (Reward identity and a shallow target) of the manuscript “Exact derandomization of logarithmic space: L = RL = BPL” (preprints/Exact-Derandomization-of-Logarithmic-Space-L-equals-RL-equals-BPL-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 103 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 15030fab23d31a4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every stage, ClPc l = Pc l − Bl(I − S). (4.29) The vectors Wl = Ble satisfy 0 ≤ Wl ≤ 1, Wl = Pc l p0 − ClPc l p0, (4.30) and their updates are Wl+1(xi) = ri(x) Wl(x) + (ElWl)(x)  . (4.31) If x̄l is the all-primary copy of a base vertex x, then 0 ≤ p0(x) − Wl(x̄l) ≤ |V0| 2−(H−1)l . (4.32) Consequently there is L = O(B) for which the last upper bound is strictly less than 1/16 for every base vertex x. In particular, p0(x) = 0 implies WL(x̄L) = 0, and p0(x) ≥ 1/2 implies WL(x̄L) > 7/16. Every full stage domain has size 2O(B) and admits O(B)-bit addresses.
